_metadata.rubric: owner-clarified rubric with calibration anchors + no-literal-false-facts reminder, 2026-10-18
_metadata.independence: I read only u30-blind-input.json; no other repository file, search, web source or paid API was consulted.

hints.reason: SHARK via the compound 'loan shark'; QUEEN has no recognizable loan route, so it is one-sided filler.
SHARK via 'reef shark'; QUEEN only through niche reef species (queen angelfish, queen conch) that few players would reach.

best_available.why: At least both words share a sea setting (reef shark; queen angelfish/conch on reefs), whereas LOAN gives QUEEN nothing.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; the QUEEN side is the problem for both hints.

hints.reason: SNAKE via Medusa's snake hair; QUEEN only through minor routes (Marvel's Medusa, queen of the Inhumans, or rare myth variants), since the Gorgon is not usually a queen.
QUEEN as the famous queen of Egypt; SNAKE via the well-known story of her death by asp bite.
SNAKE directly (an asp is a snake); QUEEN via the familiar Cleopatra-and-the-asp story.

best_available.why: One famous story lands squarely on both words.

pairs.pair_note: ASP depends on the same Cleopatra scene.

hints.reason: SPIDER via Tolkien's giant spider Shelob; she is not a queen, so the QUEEN side is missing.
SPIDER via 'black widow'; QUEEN only via the idea of a widowed queen (dowager, Victoria in mourning), which is a stretch.

best_available.why: Black widow is a strong spider route and widowed queens give a faint QUEEN link; SHELOB has none.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS.

hints.reason: QUEEN via 'queen bee'; SPRING only via the seasonal scene of bees among spring flowers, which is loose.
QUEEN via the May Queen of May Day festivals; SPRING because May is a spring month.

best_available.why: May Queen plus May as a spring month reaches both words.

pairs.pair_note: BEE is strong for QUEEN but thin for SPRING.

hints.reason: QUEEN via 'beauty queen'; STAR has no familiar beauty phrase or scene, only vague glamour.
QUEEN via 'prom queen'; STAR has no recognizable prom route.
STAR via 'shooting star'; QUEEN only if the player recalls the band Queen's 'Don't Stop Me Now', which mentions a shooting star.

best_available.why: The only hint that reaches both words at all, through the Queen song; the other two give STAR nothing.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; BEAUTY and PROM are QUEEN-only.

hints.reason: TRAIN as the long trailing back of a gown; QUEEN via the familiar scene of a queen's ceremonial gown.
QUEEN is royal; TRAIN via the Royal Train or a royal gown's train, which works at moderate strength.
QUEEN via coronation robes; TRAIN as the long train those robes trail.

best_available.why: A queen's gown with a long train is one clear picture.

pairs.pair_note: GOWN and ROBE use the same route.

hints.reason: QUEEN as a royal lady; WATER only via the Arthurian Lady of the Lake, so both sides are weak.
WATER as the mermaid's home; QUEEN only via folklore and fantasy mermaid or sea queens, which is not a fixed familiar figure.

best_available.why: Strong on WATER, with at least a fairy-tale sea-queen image for QUEEN.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS.

hints.reason: Snow White story: the Evil Queen, disguised as an old witch-like hag, offers the poisoned apple.
QUEEN via 'Evil Queen'; WITCH via the stock evil or wicked witch.
WITCH via Narnia's White Witch (who rules as queen); QUEEN via the White Queen of Through the Looking-Glass and Narnia's self-styled queen.

best_available.why: The Snow White apple scene joins the queen and the witch in one story.

pairs.pair_note: A strong pair; all three hints work.

hints.reason: WOLF via 'alpha wolf'; QUEEN only via the loose idea of a queen as the dominant 'alpha female'.
WOLF via House Stark's direwolf sigil in Game of Thrones; QUEEN via Sansa Stark becoming Queen in the North.

best_available.why: One franchise covers both words: direwolves and a Stark queen.

pairs.pair_note: STARK only works for Game of Thrones viewers, so this is a moderate pass.

hints.reason: RING via the smart-ring gadget; ROBOT via the loose idea of smart machines; neither side is firm.
ROBOT via robot battles (BattleBots-style shows); RING via the fighting ring or arena where battles happen.
RING via 'boxing ring'; ROBOT via boxing robots (Rock 'Em Sock 'Em Robots, Real Steel).

best_available.why: The boxing ring is certain, and boxing robots are a familiar toy and film image.

pairs.pair_note: BATTLE and BOXING both use the fighting-ring scene.

hints.reason: RING via the stone set in a ring; ROCK because stone is a near-synonym of rock.
RING via the diamond ring; ROCK via 'rock' as familiar slang for a diamond.
RING via 'engagement ring'; ROCK via the slang 'rock' for the engagement diamond.

best_available.why: Diamond ring plus 'rock' as slang for a diamond: clean on both sides.

pairs.pair_note: STONE is nearly a synonym of ROCK; keep it below the slang routes.

hints.reason: RING via the gold ring; ROSE via 'rose gold'.
RING via 'wedding ring'; ROSE via the familiar wedding scene of roses in bouquets.
The nursery rhyme 'Ring a Ring o' Roses' (pocket full of posies) names both words.

best_available.why: The nursery rhyme puts ring and roses side by side.

pairs.pair_note: A strong pair.

hints.reason: RING because a ring is a circle (near-synonym); SALT via the folklore and horror trope of a protective salt circle, which is moderate at best.
SALT via the salted rim of a margarita glass; RING only because a rim is ring-shaped.

best_available.why: Ring is a circle and a salt circle is a known trope; RIM is stronger for SALT but thinner for RING.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; a close call between the two hints.

hints.reason: Lord of the Rings: the One Ring was forged in Mordor, 'where the shadows lie' in the famous ring verse.
SHADOW as the shadow cast in an eclipse; RING via the 'ring of fire' of an annular eclipse.
RING as Sauron's One Ring; SHADOW via Sauron as 'the Shadow' looming over Middle-earth.

best_available.why: The ring verse places the Ring in Mordor, land of shadow.

pairs.pair_note: ECLIPSE is the one route that does not depend on the franchise.

hints.reason: SHARK via its rows of teeth; RING via the teething ring (ordinary inflection).
SHARK via 'card shark'; RING only via boxing's ring-card holders, which is a weaker phrase.

best_available.why: Shark teeth are certain and the teething ring is a familiar object.

pairs.pair_note: A moderate pair.

hints.reason: Both words only through the real but little-known species name 'ring-necked snake'.
SNAKE because snakes coil; RING only because a coil is a run of ring-like loops.
The ouroboros is a snake eating its own tail, forming a ring.

best_available.why: One image is both a snake and a ring.

pairs.pair_note: OUROBOROS is a less common word, but the image is exact.

hints.reason: SPIDER via the orb-weaver; an orb is a sphere, not a ring, so RING gets only a vague round-shape link.
SPIDER via its web; RING only via the old internet 'webring' or the concentric rings of an orb web.

best_available.why: A spider web's concentric rings and 'webring' give a faint RING link; ORB has none.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS.

hints.reason: RING via ringing a bell; SPRING has no recognizable bell phrase or scene.
SPRING because a spring is a coil; RING only because a coil is a run of ring-shaped loops.

best_available.why: Exact for SPRING and a shape link to RING; BELL gives SPRING nothing.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS.

hints.reason: RING because a halo is a ring of light; STAR only via halos around bright sky objects or starry haloes in religious art.
RING via Saturn's rings; STAR only through the shared night-sky and astronomy scene, since Saturn is a planet, not a star (it must not be explained as one).

best_available.why: Saturn's rings are certain, and Saturn shines like a star in the night sky.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. SATURN must be explained as a night-sky scene, not as a star.

hints.reason: RING via 'wedding ring'; TRAIN via the long train of a wedding dress.
RING as what a bell does; TRAIN via the locomotive's bell or the crossing bell.

best_available.why: Both words are wedding items: the ring and the dress train.

pairs.pair_note: A good pair.

hints.reason: WATER fills a bathtub; RING via the familiar 'bathtub ring' of grime at the waterline.
RING via the ring buoy or life ring; WATER because buoys float on water.
Ripples are the expanding rings on a water surface.

best_available.why: One picture shows both: rings spreading on water.

pairs.pair_note: A strong pair.

hints.reason: RING via the 'fairy ring' of mushrooms (also called a witches' ring); WITCH via that folklore and the shared magical-folk scene.
RING via the magic ring of fairy tales and Tolkien; WITCH as a practitioner of magic.
WITCH casts spells; RING only via enchanted rings, a weaker step than MAGIC.

best_available.why: Magic ring and witch's magic both land directly.

pairs.pair_note: FAIRY is nice for players who know the 'witches' ring' name.

hints.reason: RING as a near-synonym of circle; WOLF only via wolves circling their prey (verb), a moderate image.
WOLF via its howl; RING has no route except the vague sense of a sound ringing out.

best_available.why: Ring = circle, plus wolves circling prey; HOWL is WOLF-only.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS.

hints.reason: ROSE via the enchanted rose in Beauty and the Beast; ROBOT has no beast route.
ROBOT via Pixar's WALL-E; the film's key plant is a seedling, not a rose, so a rose link would be a false fact.
ROBOT via Rosie, the Jetsons' robot maid; ROSE via Rosie as a pet form of the name Rose.

best_available.why: A famous robot whose name is a form of Rose.

pairs.pair_note: ROSIE does not contain the letters ROSE in order, so it is not a contains_target failure.

hints.reason: Shared property: salt speeds up rusting of metal, and metal robots rust (cause and effect).
SALT via 'salt shaker'; ROBOT has no shaker route.

best_available.why: Salt causes rust and robots suffer it, so RUST is a real link between the two.

pairs.pair_note: RUST is only a moderate pass.

hints.reason: SHADOW copies your every move; ROBOT via robots and androids that mimic human movement, a shared copying property.
SHADOW via 'shadow puppet'; ROBOT only via the loose idea of a controlled mechanical figure.

best_available.why: Shadows and robots both copy human movement.

pairs.pair_note: MIMIC is a weak pass; a second opinion would help.

hints.reason: ROBOT is mechanical; SHARK via the famously troublesome mechanical shark used to film Jaws.
SHARK via the film Jaws; ROBOT only via that film's animatronic shark prop, which is a step removed.

best_available.why: Names the robot quality directly and recalls the mechanical Jaws shark.

pairs.pair_note: Both hints rely on the Jaws prop for one side.

hints.reason: ROBOT via 'robot arm'; SNAKE only via the snake-like flex of such arms (snake-arm robots are niche).
SNAKE slithers; ROBOT has no ordinary slither route.

best_available.why: Strong for ROBOT, with a faint snake-like-motion link; SLITHER is SNAKE-only.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS.

hints.reason: SPIDER as a crawler; ROBOT via crawler robots and web crawlers, which are also called bots or spiders.
ROBOT because BOT is its clipped form (near-synonym, letters inside the target); SPIDER only via web-spider bots.
SPIDER via its eight legs; ROBOT only via legged and spider robots, which is loose.

best_available.why: Crawling spiders and crawler bots meet in one word.

pairs.pair_note: BOT is a clipping of ROBOT; the owner should decide whether that counts as contains_target.

hints.reason: SPRING because a spring is a coil; ROBOT only via coils inside machinery, which is vague.
ROBOT via the classic wind-up tin robot toy; SPRING because wind-up toys run on a coiled spring.

best_available.why: A wind-up robot is powered by a spring.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: ROBOT as droid; STAR via Star Wars, where droids are iconic.
STAR via 'Star Wars'; ROBOT via the TV show Robot Wars and Star Wars' droids.
ROBOT: R2-D2 is the most famous film robot; STAR via Star Wars.

best_available.why: An iconic robot from Star Wars.

pairs.pair_note: All three hints use Star Wars.

hints.reason: TRAIN via driverless metro trains; ROBOT via automated, robot-driven vehicles.
ROBOT via the Transformers robots; TRAIN only via the few Transformers that turn into trains, or electrical transformers on railways, which is niche.

best_available.why: Automated trains are a real robot-like scene.

pairs.pair_note: A moderate pair.

hints.reason: WATER fills a pool; ROBOT only via robotic pool cleaners, a real but not obvious device.
Cause and effect: water makes metal rust, and metal robots rust.
WATER via the Tin Man rusting in the rain in The Wizard of Oz; ROBOT only by treating the tin woodman as a proto-robot, which he is not literally.

best_available.why: Water causes rust and robots rust, so RUST links both words directly.

pairs.pair_note: TINMAN's ROBOT side is a recharacterization; do not call him a robot in an explanation.

hints.reason: WITCH via The Wizard of Oz's witches; ROBOT only by treating the Tin Man as robot-like, which is a stretch.
Halloween scene: witch and robot are both classic costumes.

best_available.why: Both are stock Halloween costumes.

pairs.pair_note: TINMAN is scored the same way as in robot/water.

hints.reason: WOLF via its howl; ROBOT has no route (Howl's Moving Castle's Howl is a wizard, not a robot).
WOLF via 'wolf pack'; ROBOT gets only filler readings (battery pack, a pack of robots).

best_available.why: At least robot swarms or packs can be pictured; HOWL gives ROBOT nothing.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; both hints are WOLF-only.

hints.reason: ROSE via 'desert rose' (also the name of a rose-shaped crystal rock formation); ROCK via desert rock landscapes and that formation.
ROSE via 'rose quartz'; ROCK because quartz is a common rock-forming mineral (rock in everyday speech).
Guns N' Roses, the rock band (brand and plural route).

best_available.why: One famous rock band named with Roses.

pairs.pair_note: A strong pair.

hints.reason: SALT via 'salt mine'; ROCK as what mines dig through, including rock-salt mines.
Halite is the mineral name for rock salt, so it is exact for the compound, but the word is niche.
Winter scene: road salt, spread as rock salt on icy roads.

best_available.why: Salt mines cut through rock: one familiar place.

pairs.pair_note: HALITE is exact but obscure.

hints.reason: ROCK as what caves are made of; SHADOW via dark caves and Plato's cave of shadows.
SHADOW because shade is a near-synonym; ROCK only via shade cast by a rock, which is weak.

best_available.why: A rock cave full of shadows, plus Plato's allegory.

pairs.pair_note: Fine.

hints.reason: ROCK via Alcatraz's nickname 'The Rock'; SHARK only via the popular legend of shark-filled waters blocking escapes. The bay's sharks are mostly small and harmless, so an explanation must call it a legend, not a fact.
SHARK via 'reef shark'; ROCK via rocky reefs.

best_available.why: A reef is a rock-and-coral place where reef sharks live.

pairs.pair_note: ALCATRAZ is clever but leans on a myth for SHARK.

hints.reason: Familiar scene: a snake basking on a sun-warmed rock.
Rule failure: the hint contains the target SNAKE.
SNAKE because a python is one; ROCK via the rock python (for example the African rock python).

best_available.why: A snake on a rock is one picture.
